prime_advertising.contractor: Argonaut Constructors, Inc.  Contact: Adrianna Wagner  Address: PO Box 639,  Santa Rosa, CA 95402  Phone: +1 (707) 542-4862  Fax: N/A  Email: awagner@argonautconstructors.com   Services needed: Argonaut Constructors, Inc. is looking for qualified subcontractors and suppliers for a wide range of work. Available opportunities include traffic control, stormwater management, safety upgrades, erosion control, and signing and striping enhancements.  Lead Compliance Plan, full Traffic Control Systems and Construction Area Signs, Portable Changeable Message Signs, Radar Speed Feedback Sign Systems, and a range of Temporary Traffic Management elements such as pavement markings, barriers, and crash cushions. Environmental protection measures include Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP), Hydraulic Mulch Applications, Fiber Rolls, Check Dams, Drainage Inlet Protection, Street Sweeping, and Concrete Washouts. Permanent work items include Hot Mix Asphalt Dikes, Sign Structures (Truss and Bridge Mounted), Concrete Barrier Transitions, Guardrail Systems, Crash Cushions, Concrete Curb, Sidewalk, and Ditch Lining, Gross Solids Removal Devices, and Lighting and Signal System Modifications. The project further includes Thermoplastic Traffic Striping with Enhanced Wet Night Visibility, Reflective Pavement Markers, Roadside Sign Installation and Removal, and Traffic Management System Maintenance.  Interested subcontractors and suppliers are encouraged to reach out to join a team dedicated to delivering high-quality, safe, and efficient project results.  Requirements: Argonaut Constructors, Inc. is dedicated to supporting our partners by offering assistance with bid preparation and scope clarifications, guidance on bonding, insurance, and technical requirements, and by dividing work into smaller, manageable packages. For questions or more information, please contact Joey Ramirez (Estimator) at jramirez@argonautconstructors.com and estimating@argonautconstructors.com, or call (707) 542-4862. Subcontractors must have insurance listing Argonaut as Additional Insured, provide Payment and Performance Bonds for contracts over $25,000, and participate in union agreements if non-signatory. Argonaut Constructors is an Equal Opportunity Employer, providing fair consideration to all applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.  Date posted: 2025-11-13 10:56:11

bidder_inquiries.inquiry_title: Inquiry #1: Bid Item 47 - Structural Concrete, Box Culvert -
bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #1: Bid Item 47 - Structural Concrete, Box Culvert -Bid Item 47 is for a Structural Concrete, Box Culvert. Furthermore, there is no item for reinforcing steel for a CIP, Structural Concrete Box Culvert. 
Plan Sheets 5 and 20 call out for an 8.0' x 8.0' Precast RCB Culvert. 
Will the State please indicate which type of RCB they would like?Inquiry submitted: 2025-11-11 17:10:44

bidder_inquiries.inquiry_title: Inquiry #2: Bid Item 12 - Request for Clarification -
bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #2: Bid Item 12 - Request for Clarification -Bid Item 12 is for Temporary Erosion Control Blanket. Standard Specification section 13-5.02B states "An erosion control blanket must comply with the specifications for RECPs in section 21-2.02O except section 21-2.01 does not apply."

The quantity for Bid Item 12 is 13,500 square yards (121,500 square feet). What is the intent of Bid Item 12 when bid item 36, Rolled Erosion Control Product gets installed permanently and is the same material as bid item 12?

It seems unnecessary and wasteful to install this quantity of RECP for Bid Item 12, only to remove it and reinstall a lesser quantity permanently. Moreover, there is a temporary EC item for BFM.

Will the State please clarify the intent of Bid Item 12 or remove it from the bid item list?Inquiry submitted: 2025-11-13 10:51:30
responses: Response 1: (BI#2) - Your inquiry has been received and is being reviewed. Inquiries submitted within two business days of bid opening are not guaranteed a response.Response posted 2025-11-13 11:29:18

Will the State please review Bid Item 14.Inquiry submitted: 2025-11-13 10:56:49

bidder_inquiries.inquiry_title: Inquiry #1: Sections 6.104 & 99-13122: Buy America & Temporary Tensioned Membrane Structure -
bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #1: Sections 6.104 & 99-13122: Buy America & Temporary Tensioned Membrane Structure -Regarding Section 6.104 and 99-13122: I noticed the Buy America section in the bid specifications and wonder if it is applicable to the temporary Sprung Structure. While the aluminum arches and poly membrane would be categorized as 6-1.04E Construction Materials, does Buy America not apply to the temporary Sprung as it is temporary work that is not incorporated into the finished product (6-1.04A)?

While Sprung does qualify under FAR 25.101(a) of the Buy American Act, we do not qualify under Buy America standards in 2 CFR 184.6 as this requires 100% US sourcing and manufacturing.  We can provide membrane that is Berry Amendment qualified, but many of our parts are sourced internationally.Inquiry submitted: 2025-11-11 09:40:08

prime_advertising.contractor: Argonaut Constructors, Inc.  Contact: Adrianna Wagner  Address: PO Box 639,  Santa Rosa, CA 95402  Phone: +1 (707) 542-4862  Fax: N/A  Email: awagner@argonautconstructors.com   Services needed: Argonaut Constructors, Inc. is looking for qualified subcontractors and suppliers for a wide range of work. Available opportunities include traffic control and safety such as lead compliance plans, construction area signs, traffic control systems, temporary pavement markings, channelizers, radar speed feedback signs, temporary barriers, changeable message signs, and crash cushions. Work is also available in environmental and site management, including job site management, water pollution control programs, drainage inlet protection, fiber rolls, street sweeping, concrete washouts, treated wood waste, noise monitoring, wood mulch, and compost. Concrete and masonry scopes include structural concrete for drainage inlets, minor concrete for curbs, gutters, sidewalks, driveways, textured paving, and masonry retaining walls. Additional opportunities include signing and pavement marking (removal and installation of roadside signs, aluminum panels, pavement markers, mast-arm installations, and thermoplastic traffic stripes with enhanced wet night visibility) as well as signal and lighting system work. Interested subcontractors and suppliers are encouraged to reach out to join a team dedicated to delivering high-quality, safe, and efficient project results.  Requirements: Argonaut Constructors, Inc. is dedicated to supporting our partners by offering assistance with bid preparation and scope clarifications, guidance on bonding, insurance, and technical requirements, and by dividing work into smaller, manageable packages. For questions or more information, please contact Tommy Doherty (Estimator) at tdoherty@argonautconstructors.com and estimating@argonautconstructors.com, or call (707) 542-4862. Subcontractors must have insurance listing Argonaut as Additional Insured, provide Payment and Performance Bonds for contracts over $25,000, and participate in union agreements if non-signatory. Argonaut Constructors is an Equal Opportunity Employer, providing fair consideration to all applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.  Date posted: 2025-11-04 13:49:02

Work is also available in environmental and site management, including job site management, water pollution control programs, drainage inlet protection, fiber rolls, street sweeping, concrete washouts, treated wood waste, noise monitoring, wood mulch, and compost. Concrete and masonry scopes include structural concrete for drainage inlets, minor concrete for curbs, gutters, sidewalks, driveways, textured paving, and masonry retaining walls. Additional opportunities include signing and pavement marking (removal and installation of roadside signs, aluminum panels, pavement markers, mast-arm installations, and thermoplastic traffic stripes with enhanced wet night visibility) as well as signal and lighting system work. Interested subcontractors and suppliers are encouraged to reach out to join a team dedicated to delivering high-quality, safe, and efficient project results.  Requirements: Argonaut Constructors, Inc. is dedicated to supporting our partners by offering assistance with bid preparation and scope clarifications, guidance on bonding, insurance, and technical requirements, and by dividing work into smaller, manageable packages. For questions or more information, please contact Tommy Doherty (Estimator) at tdoherty@argonautconstructors.com and estimating@argonautconstructors.com, or call (707) 542-4862. Subcontractors must have insurance listing Argonaut as Additional Insured, provide Payment and Performance Bonds for contracts over $25,000, and participate in union agreements if non-signatory. Argonaut Constructors is an Equal Opportunity Employer, providing fair consideration to all applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.  Date posted: 2025-11-04 13:49:02

bidder_inquiries.inquiry_title: Inquiry #3: 9-1.08 PAYMENT ADJUSTMENTS FOR FUEL PRICE INDEX FLUCTUATIONS -
bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #3: 9-1.08 PAYMENT ADJUSTMENTS FOR FUEL PRICE INDEX FLUCTUATIONS -Will the State please include specification section 9-1.08 Payment Adjustments for Fuel Price Index Fluctuations to address any potential issues in regard to a shortage in oil supply on future contracts?  Reference below:

Replace Reserved in section 9-1.08 with:
9-1.08 PAYMENT ADJUSTMENTS FOR FUEL PRICE INDEX FLUCTUATIONS
9-1.08A General
Section 9-1.08 applies to fuel payment adjustments to applicable contract item payments. Section 9-1.08
does not apply if you opted out of fuel payment adjustments for price index fluctuations at time of bid.
The Engineer adjusts applicable contract item payments whenever the California statewide fuel price
index for the month that a bid item payment is included in a monthly progress estimate for completed
work is more than 15 percent higher or lower than the price index at time of bid.
The Department determines the California statewide fuel price index each month on or about the 5th day
of the month using the average posted prices for diesel in effect for the previous month. The California
statewide fuel price index is based on prices posted by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA).
The index posting will be the average pricing for the previous month. Fuel price index monthly averages
include all taxes as stated by the EIA. Obtain the California statewide fuel price index from the following
site:

http://www.dot.ca.gov/hq/construc/dieselindex/Inquiry submitted: 2025-10-16 10:08:57
responses: Response 1: bidder inquiry is in-reviewResponse posted 2025-10-17 01:31:51
Response 2: bid per plansResponse posted 2025-10-21 00:58:28

bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #1: Digouts (Sheet C-1 and Q-3) -Please reference the above sheets.  There is not enough information to bid the digout scope of work.  At minimum, we need to know: the location, the length, and the width of each digout similar to what is generally provided by the State.

The current plans (Sheet C-1) only provide a generic typical detail showing potential size and layout.  The Repair Failed Area table on Sheet Q-3 only provides generic descriptions such as "#1, #2 Lanes & Right Shoulder" along with quantity totals between certain post miles.  

We need more specific information in order to properly bid this item.  Please provide the specific location (i.e. #1 lane, #2 lane, shoulder, etc.), length, and width (6-ft or 12-ft) of each digout.Inquiry submitted: 2025-11-10 14:07:11

prime_advertising.contractor: Disney Construction, Inc.  Contact: Vincent Diep  Address: 533 Airport Blvd STE 120,  Burlingame  Phone: +1 (415) 680-7752  Fax: N/A  Email: vdiep@disneyconstruction.com   Services needed: Disney Construction, Inc. is requesting quotes from all qualified subcontractors and suppliers including certified DBE (Disabled Business Enterprises) firms for the following items of work, including but not limited to: Traffic Control, Traffic Control Equipment, Construction Area Signs, SWPPP, Erosion Control, Clear & Grub, Demolition, Temp Fence, Signage, Fencing, Striping, Asphalt Paving/Grinding, Excavation/Backfill, Utility/Drainage Trenching, Structural Concrete, Rebar, CIDH/Drilling, Barrier Rail, Guard Rail, Signage, Street Sweeping, Trucking and Offhauling, Landscaping, Concrete Pumping, Material Supply & Equipment Rental. Disney Construction encourages subcontractors and suppliers submitting prices to utilize DBE businesses whenever possible. This may be accomplished through second tier subcontracting, owner-operator equipment, or the purchase of supplies.  Requirements: Disney Construction Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is requesting quotes from all qualified subcontractors and suppliers. Disney Construction Inc. is willing to breakout portions of work to encourage DBE/MBE/WBE/SBE/DVBE participation. Please contact us if you need assistance with the following: (a) Contacting bonding and/or insurance companies, (b) Arranging with sureties incremental or phased bonding for DBE, MBE, WBE, SBE & DVBEs, (c) Paying for the cost of the bond insurance, (d) Waving bonding or insurance requirements, (e) Referrals to Business Development Centers for obtaining bonding, insurance, or lines of credit, (f) assistance and coordination with construction equipment procurement/rental if needed, (g) procuring material or supplies . 100% performance and payment bonds with a surety company subject to approval of Disney Construction, Inc. are required of subcontractors for this project. Disney Construction, Inc. will pay bond premium up to 1.5%. Subcontractor must possess a valid contractor's license, current insurance, worker's compensation meeting Disney Construction's requirement and be registered under Public Works Contractors Registration Law [SB 854]. Subcontractors will be required to abide by terms and conditions of the AGC Master Labor Agreements and to execute an agreement utilizing the latest DCI Subcontract incorporating prime contract terms and conditions, including payment provisions. Disney Construction is signatory to the Laborers, Carpenters, and Operator Engineers. Disney Construction, Inc.'s listing of a subcontractor is not to be construed as an acceptance of all the subcontractor's conditions or exceptions included with the subcontractor's price quote. Please send in your scope letters 2 days prior to bid day and your quote 24 hours prior to bid. Please contact Vincent Diep at (415) 680-7752 or Dyon Zaratian at (650) 259-9545 ext. 2513 with any questions, or email estimating@disneyconstruction.com. Please note that all Contractors and subcontractors must register with The DIR (Department of Industrial Relations) in order to bid on public works projects. Include CSLB License Number and DIR Number on All Quotes Submitted. Plans and specifications can be reviewed at our main office located at 533 Airport Blvd Suite #120 Burlingame CA. Please call to setup an appointment for review.  Date posted: 2025-11-05 07:48:21

bidder_inquiries.question: Inquiry #1: Clarification of Bid Item #155 -For Bid Item #155:  "THERMOPLASTIC PAVEMENT MARKING (ENHANCED WET NIGHT VISIBILITY) (RECESSED)" could Caltrans please clarify whether the recessed installation must specifically be 1 inch in depth for these markings, or if an alternative depth is acceptable per standard practice or project requirements?Inquiry submitted: 2025-10-01 08:24:42

bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #13: DBE Outreach Meeting  -We are writing concerning the Caltrans meeting held on Oct 20 for the referenced project.   

The specifications included 2 Mandatory meetings, Section 2-1.05 Mandatory Prebid Meeting and Section 2-1.04 Mandatory Prebid Outreach Meeting. The Notice to Contractors specified a Mandatory Prebid Meeting on October 20 at 10:00 am. There was no date for Mandatory Pre-Bid Outreach Meeting scheduled.  These are different meetings, with a different purpose, hence 2 separate specification sections to address them.  

Addendum 1 did the following: 
1.	Deleted Section 2-1.05 – Mandatory Virtual Prebid Meeting in its entirety. 
2.	Modified Section 2-1.04 – Mandatory Virtual Prebid Outreach Meeting.   
 
Section 2-1.04, modified by Addendum 1, still did not specify a date for the Outreach Meeting.   

We did not attend the meeting on 10/20, as Addendum 1 cancelled section 2-1.05 which in effect cancelled the meeting requirement. We were advised by other contractors that a meeting was held anyway on 10/20. Our understanding from conversations with the Duty Senior is that Caltrans considers the meeting held on 10/20 at 10:00 was intended to be the Mandatory Prebid Outreach meeting specified in Section 2-1.04.

Yet, in response to bidders inquiry #8, Caltrans responded as follows:
Response 2: Contractors should expect DBE goals to be set to zero by addendum on all currently advertised projects. Kindly be reminded to attend mandatory prebid outreach meetings. Response posted 2025-10-20 14:09:28 

We note that the response was posted on 10/20 at 14:09:28, after the alleged outreach meeting held at 10:00 am on 10/20, which would confirm that the Mandatory Prebid Outreach Meeting specified in section 2-1.04 had yet to held at that time, and confirms our understanding that it is yet to be scheduled.
 
Our interpretation of the addendum was that the mandatory pre-bid meeting was cancelled, and that a future addendum would be issued giving a date for the outreach meeting.   Also, on the same date as the addendum was issued, Caltrans issued a Notice on the Contractor’s Corner Web Portal concerning the U.S. DOT IFR that implemented changes to DBE programs.  The change in Federal Requirements leads to questions regarding the legal and economic implications of having a mandatory meeting that includes outreach to DBEs. This notice stated that Caltrans is in the process of issuing addenda for all advertised projects.   An addendum on this topic has not yet been issued for this project.  Since the language in Section 2-1.04 includes DBEs we assumed that a revised spec without DBEs is forthcoming and at that time that a date would be set for an outreach meeting that excluded DBEs once the specifications were revised.
 
Given all the above facts, we respectfully request the Prebid Outreach Meeting be scheduled, or made optional in the upcoming addendum.  Absent either, we intend to take all necessary actions to protest the future award of a contract for the project.Inquiry submitted: 2025-10-24 13:35:30
responses: Response 1: The inquiry has been received and submitted for consideration.Response posted 2025-10-24 13:39:25

bidder_inquiries.inquiry_title: Inquiry #16: Galvanization of welded elements- constructability -
bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #16: Galvanization of welded elements- constructability -Sheet "Fender System Details No 1" note 3 says all steel to be galvanized. This presumably includes the steel pipe piles and walers and structural elements of the fender system. Other details depict field welds of brackets to the steel pipe piles. Some of these welds occur below the water surface. Such welding is problematic because: 
a) the galvanization must be removed in order to weld elements, and welding may be repaired by hot stick or spray methods, which is inferior to hot dip, but also it cannot be performed on the welds below water. These below water welds will be left uncoated. 
b) the quality of welds below water in low visibility and current is problematic. 
c) welded attachments prohibit economical replacement of elements that may get damaged from vessel allisions which are common on this bridge. 

For quality, constructability, and maintenance advantages, it is recommended that the waler attachment to the piles be achieved through mechanical means such as a clamp or collar system. Please provide or allow for modifications to this welded design prior to bidding.Inquiry submitted: 2025-10-29 17:07:21
responses: Response 1: The inquiry has been received and submitted for consideration.Response posted 2025-10-30 08:09:15

bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #60: Plastic Lumber Void Testing -The plastic lumber supplier has issued a standard letter which is a response to the CalTrans standard spec regarding void testing. Contractors generally do not have an alternative to resolve this issue and it causes a lengthy substitution effort during the project. We would like to get pre-bid approval to forgo void testing and standards as they are written in the standard spec. Below is the language received from the plastic lumber supplier: 

Attn Estimating, 
As the Product Manager for ... , the composite structural timber and lumber manufacturer, I want to proactively advise you of our position on the void test requirements, before lots of time and expense are invested. I can simply and emphatically state that, our Fiber & Bar Reinforced Molded Lumber (MF & MB), will not meet these requirements 100% of the time……by design. 
Unlike other HDPE products available today, the MF & MB product is a molded product i.e. the material is injected by an extruder, into the mold to define its shape, then allowed to cool. The material "sets-up" in a high-density perimeter around the mold due to the heat loss at the surfaces. This dense perimeter is what imparts the good physical properties of the MF & MB product. Commensurate with that, the interior of the mold requires the use of a foaming agent to assure the full cross-section is filled. That foamed interior is very porous as a result and anytime someone saws through the timber, that porous interior will be exposed and there maybe voids. These voids do not cause a deterioration of the performance parameters of the product. The void testing describes the need to do exactly that when slicing our boards along its length.Inquiry submitted: 2025-11-12 11:49:42
responses: Response 1: The inquiry has been received and submitted for consideration.Response posted 2025-11-12 14:25:53

bidder_inquiries.inquiry_title: Inquiry #13: 9-1.08 PAYMENT ADJUSTMENTS FOR FUEL PRICE INDEX FLUCTUATIONS -
bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #13: 9-1.08 PAYMENT ADJUSTMENTS FOR FUEL PRICE INDEX FLUCTUATIONS -Will the State please include specification section 9-1.08 Payment Adjustments for Fuel Price Index Fluctuations to address any potential issues in regard to a shortage in oil supply on future contracts?  Reference below:

Replace Reserved in section 9-1.08 with:
9-1.08 PAYMENT ADJUSTMENTS FOR FUEL PRICE INDEX FLUCTUATIONS
9-1.08A General
Section 9-1.08 applies to fuel payment adjustments to applicable contract item payments. Section 9-1.08
does not apply if you opted out of fuel payment adjustments for price index fluctuations at time of bid.
The Engineer adjusts applicable contract item payments whenever the California statewide fuel price
index for the month that a bid item payment is included in a monthly progress estimate for completed
work is more than 15 percent higher or lower than the price index at time of bid.
The Department determines the California statewide fuel price index each month on or about the 5th day
of the month using the average posted prices for diesel in effect for the previous month. The California
statewide fuel price index is based on prices posted by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA).
The index posting will be the average pricing for the previous month. Fuel price index monthly averages
include all taxes as stated by the EIA. Obtain the California statewide fuel price index from the following
site:

http://www.dot.ca.gov/hq/construc/dieselindex/Inquiry submitted: 2025-10-16 10:18:25

bidder_inquiries.inquiry_title: Inquiry #1: Bid Item 049- JOINTED PLAIN CONCRETE PAVEMENT (RSC) vs CRCP Details -
bidder_inquiries.question: Inquiry #1: Bid Item 049- JOINTED PLAIN CONCRETE PAVEMENT (RSC) vs CRCP Details -Layout sheet L1 indicates a legend of 0.95' JPCP (RSC) / 0.25' HMA (Type A), which aligns with the quantities listed on sheet Q-2 and the bid item description. However, several detail pages show a section of 0.95' CRCP / 0.25' HMA, which contradicts the layout sheets. Please confirm that the following detail sheets are incorrect: C-53 through C-60, C-87, C-89, and C-90. Additionally, please verify that this project will not include any CRCP and modify the aforementioned detail sheets accordingly.Inquiry submitted: 2025-10-09 09:48:54
responses: Response 1: Your inquiry has been submitted for review.Response posted 2025-10-13 14:06:08

Subcontractors must possess a current contractor's license, DIR registration number, insurance, and workers compensation coverage meeting Granite's requirements, and will be required to sign the standard Granite subcontract agreement. A copy of the insurance requirements and agreement can be obtained by contacting the Estimator. Please call if you need assistance in obtaining bonding, insurance, equipment, materials, and/or supplies. Granite intends to work cooperatively with all qualified firms seeking work on this project. All quotes are subject to the terms of Granite Construction Company's applicable standard form agreement which is available through the following link: https://www.graniteconstruction.com/ca-resources/quote-solicitation . Granite is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  Date posted: 2025-09-27 08:27:10

99-16620A  General 
99-16620A(1)  Summary

Where in relation to the existing Storage Unit masonry walls is this wrought iron fence installed?  Is it in the sidewalk immediately in front of the storage unit masonry walls?  It appears many areas shown at this location already have wrought iron fencing.  Please clarify.

bidder_inquiries.question:
Inquiry #1:  -Is Caltrans willing to consider bids that reflect the following value engineering recycling solutions:
- Pavement Structural Section 3 features 1.00' HMA type A to be placed primarily in the SB inside shoulder 
--We would like to recycle [via a cold central plant recycling (CCPR) process] 0.75' of that 1.00' total depth and cap that recycled material with 0.25' HMA type A. We can work with Caltrans HQ regarding design equivalence, this work would be governed by Caltrans Standard Spec 30-7. Is this acceptable?

- Pavement Structural Sections 1 & 2 feature rigid pavements over HMA, which is over 0.35' AS (and I believe most of this section also requires soil stabilization) 
--We would like to replace the subbase [0.35' AS layer] by recycling the remaining pavement base materials (post excavation) in-place in a full-depth recycling process to a depth of 0.75', following Caltrans Standard Spec 30-4. We can work with Caltrans HQ regarding design equivalence. Is this acceptable? (Original Inquiry Date: 2025-09-18)Inquiry submitted: 2025-09-26 18:36:49
responses: Response 1: Please refer to Section 4-1.07 "Value Engineering" of the Standard Specifications and bid in accordance with the current contract documents. (Original Response Date:  2025-09-23)Response posted 2025-09-26 18:42:38

bidder_inquiries.question: Inquiry #8:  -Please clarify how many lane closures in one direction of travel are allowed?  Is the maximum lane closure distance on the highway the same as it is for City streets at 3000'?  Is the minimum distance between lane closures in a single direction on the highway 500'? (Original Inquiry Date: 2025-09-23)Inquiry submitted: 2025-09-26 18:37:00
responses: Response 1: (BI#9) - Your inquiry has been received and is being reviewed. Inquiries submitted within two business days of bid opening are not guaranteed a response. (Original Response Date:  2025-09-24)Response posted 2025-09-26 18:42:39

Response 2: (BI#9) - 1.	Please clarify how many lane closures in one direction of travel are allowed?  
Please refer to specification 12-4.02C(7) paragraph 2,  "Not more than 1 stationary closure in each direction of travel at one time."

2.	Is the maximum lane closure distance on the highway the same as it is for City streets at 3000'?  
Please refer to charts G1-G3 for freeway lane requirements.  Freeway lane closures are allowed without a maximum length.  Note that these are daily closures and must be removed at the end of shift of no active construction is occurring.  
Chart M1 City street lane requirements, the maximum closure length of 3000' is for flagging.  

3.	Is the minimum distance between lane closures in a single direction on the highway 500'?  
Please refer to specification 12-4.02C(7)(b) par2, "For a traffic control system with multiple work areas, place a stationary impact attenuator at each work area with a separation distance of at least 500 feet from the adjacent work area" 
The 500' is in reference to stationary impact attenuator (IAV) placement. The IAV placement discusses multiple work areas, but that would be multiple work locations within the same lane closure for a direction of travel.  No minimum distance between stationary closures on 101 because only one is allowed.Response posted 2025-10-01 11:38:15

prime_advertising.contractor: Argonaut Constructors, Inc.  Contact: Adrianna Wagner  Address: 360 Sutton Place,  Santa Rosa, CA 95407  Phone: +1 (707) 542-4862  Fax: N/A  Email: awagner@argonautconstructors.com   Services needed: Argonaut Constructors, Inc. is seeking qualified DBE/WBE/MBE subcontractors and suppliers for a highway construction project, which includes a range of activities such as the development of a Lead Compliance Plan, installation of Construction Area Signs, Traffic Control Systems, and Stationary Impact Attenuator Vehicles. The project also involves the placement of Channelizers, Traffic Drums, and Portable Radar Speed Feedback Signs, as well as the setup of Temporary Barrier Systems and Changeable Message Signs. In addition, there will be significant stormwater management tasks, including the creation of a Pollution Prevention Plan, Stormwater Sampling and Analysis, and the preparation of Annual Reports. Key tasks also include the installation of Guardrails, Concrete Barriers, and Pavement Markings, along with the removal of existing road features such as Pavement Markers, Delineators, and Crash Cushions. The project will also require extensive work with Asphalt, Concrete, and Thermoplastic Pavement Markings, as well as various Traffic Stripe Tapes and Rumble Strips. Lastly, additional work will involve Signal and Lighting System Modifications and Traffic Monitoring Station Systems. Subcontractors and suppliers are encouraged to submit bids for these and other vital components of the project.  Requirements: Argonaut Constructors, Inc. is committed to promoting diversity and supporting DBE/WBE/MBE firms by offering assistance with bid preparation, scope clarifications, bonding, insurance, and technical requirements, as well as breaking work into smaller, manageable packages. For more information or questions, contact Tommy Doherty (Estimator) at tdoherty@argonautconstructors.com or estimating@argonautconstructors.com, or call (707) 542-4862. Requirements include insurance with Argonaut as Additional Insured, Payment & Performance Bonds for contracts over $25,000, and union participation for non-signatory subcontractors. Argonaut Constructors is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive workplace.  Date posted: 2025-09-26 18:31:04
